name: Lemon-Garlic Chicken Thighs with Roasted Broccoli and Rice Pilaf
description: Sheet-pan chicken thighs with lemon, garlic, and crisp skin, roasted alongside broccoli and served with a buttery rice pilaf. Cook extra thighs — they become Tuesday's tacos.
ingredients: 2 lemons (1 sliced into rounds, 1 for juice)
1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
1/2 cup orzo or broken spaghetti (optional, for the pilaf)
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat the thighs very dry — wet skin steams instead of crisping.
Season the thighs all over with salt, pepper, and paprika. Let them sit at room temperature while the oven heats.
Arrange the thighs skin-side up on a sheet pan with the smashed garlic and lemon rounds tucked around them. Drizzle with 2 Tbsp olive oil.
Roast 25 minutes. While that happens, start the pilaf: melt 2 Tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium, add the onion and orzo, and stir until the orzo is golden, about 3 minutes.
Add the rice, stir to coat, then pour in the broth and a big pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, cover, drop to low, and cook 18 minutes. Kill the heat and let it sit covered another 5.
Toss the broccoli with the remaining olive oil, salt, and pepper. After the chicken's first 25 minutes, add the broccoli to the pan in a single layer around the thighs.
Roast another 12–15 minutes, until the thighs read 175°F and the broccoli has charred edges.
Squeeze the juice of the second lemon over everything straight out of the oven. Fluff the pilaf with the last Tbsp of butter and the parsley.
tips: Thighs are forgiving — 175°F is better than 165°F here, since the connective tissue needs the extra heat to soften.
Pull 2–3 thighs before saucing or squeezing lemon over them, cool, and refrigerate whole. Shred them cold on Tuesday; the meat pulls apart more cleanly straight from the fridge.
If the skin isn't as dark as you want at the end, run the broiler for 2 minutes and stand there watching it.
